title: Modernize GPU autoscaler reconciliation and capacity planner simplification
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: What: Replace the current multi-loop autoscaler reconciliation logic with a single, event-driven reconciler and simplify the capacity planner’s heuristic layers. Why: Current codebase has diverged with multiple partial reconcilers, heavy lock contention, and layered heuristics that create race conditions and make reasoning about node lifecycle difficult. This produces increased tail latency during scale events and complicates bug fixes. Goal is to reduce code complexity, eliminate duplicated state transitions, and improve scaling latency and planner CPU overhead by ~30-40% in bench workloads.
background_and_reasoning: The existing autoscaler has three layers: lease allocator, planner heuristics, and an eventual reconciler. Over the past two years multiple hotfixes introduced guardrails and shadow behaviors (soft-evictions, lease extensions) leading to fragile interactions during rapid scale-ups. Incident telemetry (incidents/2024-11-gpu-surge) shows spikes in controller CPU and 99th percentile allocation latency when many pods request GPUs simultaneously. We will move to a single reconciler backed by an append-only event queue, canonical node state machine, and reduce planner heuristics to a prioritized scoring step. This should make behavior deterministic and easier to test.
acceptance_criteria: Single event-driven reconciler in prod branch behind feature flag 'autosc_reconciler_v2'
Remove duplicated node state transitions from old allocators and unit tests updated to cover canonical transitions
Planner CPU usage reduced >= 25% in synthetic scale tests (same load as incident replay)
Pod-to-allocation median latency improved >= 20% and 99th percentile improved >= 15% in bench runs
Migration path documented with rollback steps and metrics dashboard updated
tasks: Design: define canonical node state machine and transition table
Implement: event queue and reconciler skeleton (feature-flagged)
Refactor: collapse lease allocator and soft-reservation gateway into new reconciler
Refactor: simplify capacity planner to single prioritized scorer + decoupled snapshot reader
Add: comprehensive unit and integration tests for transitions and failure modes
Bench: replay incident trace against staging and capture metrics (latency, CPU, reconcile rate)
Rollout: gradual traffic ramp with feature flag gates and rollback monitor
Docs: runbook + migration notes + CFG knobs for tuning
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: regressions causing missed allocations under heavy churn. Mitigation: shadow mode on staging and canary clusters with request duplication for 48h before switch.
Risk: transient double-allocations during feature flip. Mitigation: idempotency tokens for allocations and cross-checker that reconciles duplicates within 30s.
Risk: performance regression in corner cases. Mitigation: maintain old reconciler behind flag for quick rollback and run regression jobs nightly during rollout.
Risk: scheduler/assume semantics mismatch. Mitigation: add integration test harness that includes kube-scheduler mocks used in production tests.
implementation_notes: Event queue will be implemented as an in-memory append-only ring with persistent tombstones in etcd for crash recovery (reuse existing queue primitives in pkg/eventq)
Canonical states: PendingReservation, Reserved, Bound, Draining, Decommissioned. Explicitly forbid state transitions not in the table; add assertion tests.
Planner will expose a 'score' function with pluggable weight vector. For now retain existing weights but remove ad-hoc overrides used in legacy code paths.
Avoid changing node lease TTL semantics; keep compatibility shim for 2 releases to help clients migrate off lease-extension calls.
testing_plan: Unit: state machine coverage >= 95% for transitions
Integration: run 10 incident-replay scenarios on staging, compare metrics against baseline
E2E: canary cluster rollout with traffic mirroring for 72 hours
Chaos: simulate partial etcd/network partitions and verify reconciler converges under mtbf conditions
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge feature-flagged reconciler into main, enable in staging only
Phase 1: Shadow mode in canary (requests duplicated) and verification for 48h
Phase 2: Gradual enable on 5% of production capacity for 24-48h with automatic rollback triggers (controller-error-rate > 2x baseline or allocation-failure-rate > 0.5%)
Phase 3: Ramp to 50% then 100% once stable for 48h; deprecate old reconciler after two successful releases
